title: Sensor error — try again in 10 min
fullDescription:
E-1 means the FreeStyle Libre reader or app could not read the sensor. Usually a transient scanning issue.

Wait 10 minutes and rescan. If persistent, sensor may need replacement.

Safety note: use fingerstick BG for critical decisions while sensor is unreadable.

fixSteps.title: Wait and rescan
fixSteps.instruction: Wait 10 minutes, scan sensor steadily 1-4cm from reader/phone.

whenToCallPro: For medical devices, contact manufacturer support or your healthcare provider before attempting service

faq.a: Hold reader 1-4cm from sensor for 1 second.

title: Sensor ended — replace
fullDescription:
E-2 indicates the sensor has reached its 14-day wear limit (or 10-day for older Libre). Apply new sensor.

Remove old sensor, insert new one, and allow 60-minute warmup.

Safety note: fingerstick BG during warmup.

fixSteps.title: Apply new sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Apply to upper arm; start via reader or app.

whenToCallPro: For medical devices, contact manufacturer support or your healthcare provider before attempting service

faq.a: 14 days for Libre 2/3, 10 days for original Libre.

title: Sensor not compatible
shortDescription: Reader or app not compatible with sensor.
fullDescription:
E-3 indicates sensor model incompatibility — e.g., using a Libre 2 sensor with a Libre 1 reader.

Verify sensor matches reader/app version; update LibreLink app if needed.

Safety note: incorrect combinations can prevent readings entirely.
whenToCallPro: For medical devices, contact manufacturer support or your healthcare provider before attempting service

faq.a: App Store or Google Play — update LibreLink.

title: Check sensor — wait 10 minutes
fullDescription:
E-4 tells you glucose readings are currently unreliable. Usually resolves within 10 minutes as sensor stabilizes.

Use fingerstick during this window.

Safety note: do not make insulin decisions from an E-4 period.

fixSteps.title: Wait
fixSteps.instruction: Wait 10 minutes, avoid pressure on sensor.

whenToCallPro: For medical devices, contact manufacturer support or your healthcare provider before attempting service

faq.a: Yes — sleeping on sensor can cause false lows.

title: Glucose below 40 mg/dL
fullDescription:
LO appears when glucose is below 40 mg/dL (2.2 mmol/L) — severe hypoglycemia.

Treat immediately with 15g fast-acting carbs and recheck in 15 minutes.

Safety note: EMERGENCY — severe hypoglycemia can cause loss of consciousness. Have someone stay with you. Call emergency services if symptoms worsen.

fixSteps.title: Recheck in 15 min
fixSteps.instruction: If still low, repeat carbs; call for help if unable to treat.

whenToCallPro: EMERGENCY: call emergency services if unable to treat or symptoms worsen
videoSearchQuery: freestyle libre LO low glucose emergency

faq.a: 15g fast carbs: 4 glucose tabs, 1/2 cup juice, or 1 tbsp honey.

title: Glucose above 400 mg/dL
fullDescription:
HI appears when glucose exceeds 400 mg/dL (22.2 mmol/L). This is severe hyperglycemia.

Check for ketones, verify with fingerstick, follow sick-day plan, and contact care team.

Safety note: URGENT — sustained HI may indicate DKA. Check urine/blood ketones.

fixSteps.title: Fingerstick verify
fixSteps.instruction: Use BG meter to confirm reading.

fixSteps.title: Follow sick-day plan
fixSteps.instruction: Correction insulin per care plan; hydrate.

whenToCallPro: URGENT: contact care team or emergency services if ketones are moderate/high or DKA symptoms appear

faq.a: Moderate-to-high ketones, vomiting, confusion, or rapid breathing.

title: Sensor failed — replace
shortDescription: Sensor failed before end of wear.
fullDescription:
Sensor Error / Replace Sensor indicates the sensor has failed prematurely. Often due to bad adhesion, application issue, or defective sensor.

Contact Abbott for warranty replacement if within wear window.

Safety note: use fingerstick until new sensor is warmed up.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Apply new sensor; save failed sensor lot number.

whenToCallPro: Contact Abbott customer care for warranty replacement

faq.a: Yes, under their Quality Guarantee — save the sensor.

title: Bluetooth signal lost (Libre 2/3)
shortDescription: Phone or reader out of range of sensor.
fullDescription:
Signal Loss means the reader/phone is out of Bluetooth range (>20 feet) or obstructed.

Move closer to sensor; check Bluetooth is on; restart LibreLink app if needed.

Safety note: during signal loss, alarms won't trigger — use fingerstick if symptomatic.

fixSteps.title: Move closer
fixSteps.instruction: Keep phone within 20 ft of sensor.

fixSteps.title: Check Bluetooth
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure Bluetooth is enabled on phone.

whenToCallPro: For medical devices, contact manufacturer support or your healthcare provider before attempting service

faq.a: Libre 3 has improved Bluetooth range vs Libre 2.

title: Reader battery low
fullDescription:
Low Battery warns that Libre reader needs charging. Reader may power off without charging.

Connect to USB charger until full.

Safety note: charge nightly to avoid interrupted monitoring.

fixSteps.title: Charge reader
fixSteps.instruction: Connect USB cable until fully charged.

whenToCallPro: For medical devices, contact manufacturer support or your healthcare provider before attempting service

title: Sensor temperature out of range
shortDescription: Environmental temperature outside sensor operating range.
fullDescription:
Sensor operates between 10-45°C. Outside this, readings pause until temperature returns.

Move to climate-controlled area; avoid hot tubs, saunas, or freezing conditions.

Safety note: readings during temperature extremes are invalid.

fixSteps.title: Move to normal temp
fixSteps.instruction: Return to room temperature; wait 10 minutes.

whenToCallPro: For medical devices, contact manufacturer support or your healthcare provider before attempting service

faq.a: Yes, up to 1m for 30 min — but avoid hot tubs.
